label: Northstar Bike Co.: three transactions
text: Alex invests $5,000 cash to start the business (assets +$5,000 cash, equity +$5,000 capital); buys a $1,200 bike repair stand on credit (assets +$1,200 equipment, liabilities +$1,200 payable); earns $300 cash from bike sales (assets +$300 cash, equity +$300 revenue).

label: Journal entry: repair stand bought for cash
text: Northstar Bike Co. pays $1,200 cash to buy a new repair stand: debit Equipment (Asset) $1,200, credit Cash (Asset) $1,200. Total debits ($1,200) = total credits ($1,200).

label: Northstar's balance sheet
text: As of December 31, 2025: Cash $8,500, Accounts Receivable $1,200, Inventory $2,300, Repair & Shop Equipment $14,000 less Accumulated Depreciation ($2,000); Total Assets $24,000. Accounts Payable $1,800, Bank Loan (long-term) $6,200, Owner's Capital $14,000, Retained Earnings $2,000; Total Liabilities + Equity $24,000. Balance check: Assets $24,000 = Liabilities $8,000 + Equity $16,000.

label: Northstar's income statement
text: Year Ended December 31, 2025: Sales Revenue $52,000 less Cost of Goods Sold ($21,000) = Gross Profit $31,000; operating expenses Wages ($14,000), Rent ($6,000), Depreciation ($2,000), Utilities & Other ($1,500); Operating Income $7,500; less Interest Expense ($500); Net Income $7,000.

label: Northstar's cash flow statement
text: Year Ended December 31, 2025. Operating: Net Income $7,000 + Depreciation (non-cash) $2,000 + Decrease in Inventory $500 less Increase in Receivables ($300) = Net Cash from Operations $9,200. Investing: Purchase of Equipment ($3,000). Financing: Owner Contribution $1,000, Loan Repayment ($1,200), net ($200). Net Change in Cash: $9,200 - $3,000 - $200 = +$6,000.

label: The custom bike build
text: Northstar Bike Co. completes a custom bike build on December 28, 2025 and invoices the client $2,000; the client pays on January 15, 2026. Cash basis records the revenue in January 2026 (when paid); accrual basis records it in December 2025 (when earned).

label: Northstar's delivery van
text: Delivery van: cost $32,000, salvage value $2,000, useful life 5 years. ($32,000 - $2,000) ÷ 5 = $6,000 per year. Book value falls from $26,000 at the end of year 1 to $2,000 at the end of year 5.

label: Northstar's ratios in action
text: Current Ratio: $12,000 ÷ $8,000 = 1.5. Debt-to-Equity: $8,000 ÷ $16,000 = 0.5. A current ratio above 1.0 and modest debt-to-equity both signal a financially healthy bike shop. A chart beside them shows two bars, 59.6 and 13.5.

label: Strong net income, low cash
text: Discussion question: Northstar Bike Co. has strong net income but low cash on hand. How is that possible, and which statement would you check first to find out?

label: Sunrise Traders Pvt. Ltd.
text: Assets: cash at bank 80,000, accounts receivable 40,000, inventory 60,000, furniture & fixtures 1,00,000 (total 2,80,000). Liabilities: accounts payable 30,000, bank loan (long-term) 1,50,000 (total 1,80,000). Equity: share capital 50,000, retained earnings (opening) 0, add net profit for the year 50,000 (total 1,00,000). Income: sales revenue 3,00,000, gain on sale of old equipment 6,000. Expenses: cost of goods sold 1,80,000, salaries expense 50,000, rent expense 24,000, loss on foreign exchange 2,000. Assets 2,80,000 = Liabilities 1,80,000 + Equity 1,00,000.

label: Om Enterprises
text: Assets: cash 50,000, accounts receivable 35,000, inventory 45,000, equipment 1,20,000, prepaid rent 5,000 (total 2,55,000). Liabilities: accounts payable 25,000, accrued salaries 10,000, long-term loan 80,000 (total 1,15,000). Equity: share capital 1,00,000 and retained earnings (opening) 10,000, plus the net profit for the year. Income: sales revenue 2,00,000, interest income 4,000. Expenses: cost of goods sold 1,20,000, salaries expense 40,000, rent expense 10,000, utilities expense 4,000. Step 3 then checks that assets equal liabilities plus equity.

label: Prepaid rent vs accrued salaries
text: Prepaid rent is an asset: cash paid in advance for a benefit not yet consumed. Accrued salaries are a liability: the benefit is already received, but cash hasn't gone out yet. Ask: has the cash moved, or has the benefit moved, and which happened first?

label: Advance received from customer (unearned revenue)
text: A liability: an obligation not yet fulfilled (goods or service still owed). Contrast with revenues from operation/sales, which is income already earned.

label: Dividend paid to shareholders
text: Equity: a distribution of profit to owners, not a cost of earning it. It reduces equity directly and never hits the income statement.

label: Outstanding electricity bill (accrued expense)
text: A liability: the expense has already been recognised on the income statement; what remains is the unpaid obligation.

label: Table 4.1: the elements of financial statements
text: A three-column table linking each Chapter 1 item (economic resource, claim, changes in resources and claims) to its element (asset, liability, equity, income, expenses) and definition, plus other changes with no element.

label: Diagram 5.1: how recognition links the elements
text: Opening statement of financial position, plus income minus expenses, plus contributions minus distributions, equals the closing statement of financial position; the middle two are the changes in equity.

label: Sale of goods for cash
text: Income is recognised from one asset (the cash) and an expense from derecognising another asset (the goods sold): the matching of costs with income.

label: Revenue information: predictive and confirmatory
text: Revenue for the current year can be used to predict revenues in future years, and can also be compared with predictions made in past years for the current year.

label: A complete depiction of a group of assets
text: A complete depiction of a group of assets includes at least a description of the nature of the assets, a numerical depiction of all of them, and what the numbers represent (historical cost or fair value).

label: Indirect verification of inventory
text: Checking the carrying amount of inventory by checking quantities and costs and recalculating the ending inventory with the same cost flow assumption, for example first-in, first-out.

label: Temporary reduction in comparability
text: Applying a new Standard prospectively can temporarily reduce comparability, which may be worthwhile to improve relevance or faithful representation in the longer term.

label: Treasury shares
text: Debt or equity instruments issued by an entity and repurchased and held by it, such as treasury shares, are not economic resources of that entity.

label: Legal ownership as a set of rights
text: Legal ownership of a physical object gives rights to use it, sell rights over it and pledge rights over it; usually accounted for as a single asset.

label: A purchased option
text: A purchased option derives its value from the chance of benefits when exercised later, but the economic resource is the present right to exercise the option, not the future benefits.

label: Principal and agent
text: An agent holding goods controlled by the principal does not have an asset, and an obligation to pass the principal's resource to a third party is not the agent's liability.

label: Salary contract before the work is done
text: A contract to pay an employee a salary for services: no present obligation to pay until the services are received; before then it is an executory contract.

label: Sale of goods for cash
text: A sale of goods for cash recognises income (from the cash asset) and an expense (from derecognising the goods sold) at the same time.

label: Property, plant and equipment and inventory
text: Property, plant and equipment and inventory are used in combination with other resources, so historical cost or current cost is likely to give relevant information about margins.

label: Holding gains and price changes
text: Under financial capital maintenance in nominal units, price increases on assets held are holding gains and conceptually profit; under physical capital maintenance they are capital maintenance adjustments within equity.
